text:
Ravi: Quick sync: the compatibility shim is still our biggest source of tail latency and memory churn. Need a plan that reduces work in the hot path, gives tenants time to migrate, and provides clear error semantics.

Eve: Can we trim the shim to only handle two legacy envelope variants and route everything else to a background rewriter? That should cut common-case allocations.

Kai: That helps. Also propose a short HTTP header `X-Format: v6` that signals clients are latest and can skip shim entirely. We'll treat absence of header as legacy.

Ravi: We'll do both: 1) fast-path header, 2) minimal inline shim for top-2 variants, 3) async rewriter for rest.

ops-bot: Created ticket INC-3999 and a dashboard stub grafana/redwood/compat-slim.

Marta: UX/Docs note: announce header and 90-day per-tenant deprecation window. Provide a console toggle to opt into "fast-path" early.

Kai: Implementation risks: zero-copy parsing may use unsafe pointers; prefer pooled buffers first, then optimize. Also add integration tests for pointer lifetimes.

Eve: For safety, add a circuit that returns 429 with `Retry-After` when rewrite queue latency > 1s. Also log `compat_path=fast|inline|async|reject`.

Ravi: Owners: Kai implements inline shim + header; Eve adds circuit + logging; Marta handles tenant comms + console. Timeline: 1 week for prototypes, 2 weeks for staged rollout.

Marta: I'll draft tenant email and console copy and post here tomorrow.

Ravi: OK let's keep updates in this thread.
